rows.subject: Surge phase presentation
rows.original_defect: Calm Building and Fading weather stills remain difficult to distinguish while Break reads mainly through darker lighting and heavier rain
rows.reason: Calm light rain, greener Building, lightning/heavier-rain Break, and Fading mist/afterglow are visibly differentiated. Full atmospheric/material finish still falls below the written bar; motion and flash rhythm are unassessed.
rows.coverage_gap: Motion, flash cadence, wind response, sound and continuous safe-radius readability.

rows.subject: creature collapse and rest
rows.original_defect: Several fainted bodies remain upright or float above the grass and some resting poses do not settle onto the ground
rows.reason: The original collapse/rest defect is still visible. Tanglevolt/fainted remains a four-legged upright wolf with the torso off the ground; Stormraven/fainted remains upright on its feet. Fulgocobra/resting is a large rolled, open-mouthed body held above the grass rather than a relaxed grounded coil. Some other resting silhouettes change substantially, but that positive change does not resolve these sampled failures.
rows.coverage_gap: One supplied snapshot per state for 14 species only. Grass obscures some exact floor contacts; no continuous fall, settlement or rest animation is assessed.

rows.subject: creature hurt and movement poses
rows.original_defect: Hurt and moving frames often retain the idle silhouette so the state is difficult to read without a filename
rows.reason: The supplied moving snapshots retain essentially the idle silhouette across the 14 sheets, including Craghorn, Sparkit, Tanglevolt and Voltarach. Hurt changes are commonly limited to a small head/torso dip, so the state is weak without its label. Several attacking snapshots lower or turn the head and read more distinctly. This is a still-image readability defect, not proof that continuous locomotion or hurt animation is absent.
rows.coverage_gap: No chronological locomotion/hurt sequence, recovery timing or actual fight exposure. Only these selected snapshots are assessed.

rows.subject: Stormheart finale
rows.original_defect: The Stormheart finale reads as a dark cylindrical ring with a hole rather than a giant living tree with a branching crown and visible core
rows.reason: Split immense tree and internal platforms are recognizable. Uniform vertical bark, blunt branch stubs, sparse crown and weak core lighting miss the reference's living-wood/stronghold finish.
rows.coverage_gap: Current calibrated distance, entrance/core detail and motion are not supplied by this five-stand heading fixture.

rows.reason: Subject not exposed by applicable current evidence; no fresh numeric severity assessment is possible.
rows.coverage_gap: Current actual Voltarach/Sparkit/trainer combat spacing; historical fight actor/cue applicability invalidated.

rows.subject: map
rows.original_defect: The map canvas shows headings and markers without visible terrain or road context for the displayed destinations
rows.reason: The displayed Stormwood map still presents large headings, Cinder Verge and a marker against an empty dark canvas/central black strip, without readable terrain contours, roads or relationships between destinations. Surveyed 0% and no destinations are explicitly shown, so I cannot claim that all explored/populated map states fail. The visible discovered-region context remains insufficient in this captured state.
rows.coverage_gap: One 0%-surveyed map state only. Explored terrain, populated destination lists, zoom/pan and other regions are unassessed.

rows.subject: normal creature scale
rows.original_defect: Several normal creatures read visibly shorter than the trainer in the shared near-framed scale view
rows.reason: Current normal-camera Sparkit reads markedly smaller/shorter than the adjacent trainer; Stormtrail also has a smaller on-screen standing extent. Many larger subjects, including Fulgocobra, Voltarach and Staticub, clearly read large, so this is not a roster-wide negative. The current world framing exposes an apparent scale-readability concern that the older normalized controls did not show. Perspective and unequal floor positions prevent an exact physical-height conclusion or a claim that geometry changed.
rows.coverage_gap: Partial apparent-scale rescore for these 14 species. Exact 1.80m-relative physical height needs equal-depth whole-body comparisons; no inferred meters, shrink operation, whole-roster or combat continuity.

rows.subject: shiny creature finish
rows.original_defect: Several shiny variants become near-uniform hot magenta and lose their ordinary species material and pattern identity
rows.reason: Most supplied shiny views replace the ordinary material separation with near-uniform intensely saturated magenta. Voltwig loses its olive/cream blocks; Craghorn and Pebbik lose ordinary pale/dark separation; Voltarach's brown plates become pink. Faces/eyes remain recognizable in several subjects and the palette is conspicuously different, but material and pattern identity are weakened. Sparkit and Stormtrail are exceptions with their ordinary palette largely retained.
rows.coverage_gap: Only one shiny standing view per species and these 14 subjects; no shiny motion, multiple lighting conditions or all-roster finish assessment.

rows.subject: menu shell
rows.original_defect: The full-screen charcoal menu with thin teal borders has little visual hierarchy or scenic connection to the illustrated world
rows.reason: The shell remains a nearly full-screen charcoal/teal rectangle with restrained flat panels and little illustrated world identity. It does have visible hierarchy: large page headings, consistently marked active tabs, selected-card borders, item art and a full creature preview. The rainy scene is faintly visible through it. The remaining issue is generic visual presentation rather than absent navigation hierarchy or unreadable text.
rows.coverage_gap: Only these captured open-menu states; no interaction, focus transitions, full content populations, device-screen or accessibility proof.

rows.subject: secondary menu panels
rows.original_defect: The Quests Build and Players panels leave most of their area empty around a few plain text lines or a single button
rows.reason: Build now has three illustrated cards, legible descriptions/costs and a clearly separated action, so the original almost-empty Build presentation is not observed. Quests has named sections and a main objective; Players has a matching trainer portrait and status, although its large central empty area and the flat text-card treatment remain visually sparse. These low-content states do not prove missing quest or multiplayer content.
rows.coverage_gap: One early quest state and solo Players state with a displayed network-port error. Populated/co-op variants, invitations or functional behavior are not assessed.

Binding rows use literal labels and their button columns shift horizontally with description length, weakening scan consistency. Most text is legible at the supplied full raster; this is scan hierarchy, not a claim that all text is unreadable. The supplied quick_bindings frame ends at the Quick items heading and shows no quick-item binding rows.
rows.coverage_gap: Quick-item binding rows below the heading are unexposed. Full settings scroll, actual rebinding, device-size reading and input behavior are unassessed.
